FRENCH — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #1
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading.

2. When practising Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.

3. When practising Informative Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Informative Speaking.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Informative Speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Informative Speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Informative Speaking.

4. When practising Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.

5. When practising Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information.

6. When practising Intensive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Listening.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Listening.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Listening.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Listening.

7. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Thank you
   B. Good night only
   C. Excuse me
   D. Good morning / hello

8. When practising Interactive speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Interactive speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Interactive speaking.

9. When practising Reading for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading for information.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for information.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for information.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading for information.

10. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. chaise
   B. porte
   C. fenêtre
   D. livre

11. When practising Persuasive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Persuasive Speaking.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Persuasive Speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Persuasive Speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Persuasive Speaking.

12. When practising Critical Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Critical Listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Critical Listening.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Critical Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Critical Listening.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Intensive Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Informative Speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Persuasive Speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for information and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for information and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Critical Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Extensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Descriptive writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
